title: Adic constructible complexes and stratified perfect local models
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that it admits a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring with a unique maximal ideal $I$ and residue field $A/I$, and assume $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\widehat A_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_X$, where the terms are constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Use categories of module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived extension of scalars [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat A_X))$, the following conditions are equivalent.

(a) $K$ is locally derived $I\widehat A_X$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete], and $K\otimes^L_{\widehat A_X}(A/I)_X\simeq\nu_X^*C$ for some bounded étale $A/I$-complex $C$ with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude. Here constructible means that each cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finitely presented $A/I$-module values [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] on a finite constructible locally closed stratification; finite Tor amplitude means that some integers $a\leq b$ satisfy $H^q(C\otimes^L_{(A/I)_X}N)=0$ for every étale $(A/I)_X$-module sheaf $N$ in degree zero and $q\notin[a,b]$.

(b) There is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] $X=\coprod_\alpha S_\alpha$ by constructible locally closed subschemes such that, on a pro-étale cover of each $S_\alpha$, $K|_{S_\alpha}$ is isomorphic to $\widehat A_{S_\alpha}\otimes_A P^\bullet$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], represented by a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules. The coefficient restriction is identified with $\widehat A_{S_\alpha}=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_{S_\alpha}$; the tensor expression means termwise extension of the constant complex $P^\bullet$.

Every complex satisfying these equivalent conditions is bounded in cohomology. These complexes form a full triangulated subcategory: it contains zero, is invariant under isomorphisms and integer shifts, and whenever two vertices of a distinguished triangle satisfy (a), so does the third. No finite dimension hypothesis on $X$ and no invertibility of residue characteristics on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and its following triangulatedness observation; Lemma 6.5.3 (boundedness); Proposition 6.6.11 (stratified perfect characterization), using Definition 6.3.1 and Remark 6.3.2 for the residue-field constructibility condition.

proof.text: Write $B_X=\widehat A_X$, $k=A/I$, and choose generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $I$, which exist since $A$ is Noetherian. First establish the precise restriction and completeness tests. For a stratum immersion $i:S\to X$, exact inverse image preserves limits, so the maps induced by the finite projections identify $i^{-1}B_X$ with $B_S=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_S$. For a pro-étale object $U\to S$, the localized site is $S_{\mathrm{proét}}/U$, so restriction is evaluation on the slice and preserves limits and exact sequences. The constant/completed coefficient lemma identifies local completeness with the unit $M\to R\lim_m(M\otimes^L Q_m)$, where $Q_m=\bigotimes_j[B\xrightarrow{a_j^m}B]$ in degrees $[-r,0]$. Exact countable products represent the derived products, and the Roos triangle computes this derived limit by the cone of $1-s$ on those products. Every $Q_m$ has finite free terms, so exact restriction commutes with its tensor complex; it commutes with the products and their cone as well. Thus restriction carries the actual completion unit to the corresponding completion unit on $S$ and on $U$. Its cone is zero if and only if its restrictions to all the chosen stratum covers are zero, by finite-stratum detection. Consequently completeness restricts to strata and their covers and is detected on any such finite family. The finite-reduction comparison in the constant/completed coefficient lemma also identifies restricted residue reduction with reduction of the restricted complex. This uses the coefficient isomorphism for immersions and slices, without identifying completed coefficients under arbitrary scheme pullback.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2), with the explicit completion-unit argument of Stacks Tags 099L (section-derived-completion-noetherian), 099M (lemma-naive-completion), 0A0E (algebraization-lemma-derived-completion-koszul), 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), and the Roos triangle.

proof.text: For later use, every bounded étale complex over the field $k=A/I$ has finite Tor amplitude. Let $C$ have cohomology in $[a,b]$ and let $N$ be an étale $k$-module sheaf in degree zero. At a geometric point $\bar x$, derived tensor pullback gives $(C\otimes^L_{k_X}N)_{\bar x}\simeq C_{\bar x}\otimes_k^L N_{\bar x}$. The point inverse image is exact, so cohomology of $C_{\bar x}$ is the stalk cohomology. Over the field $k$, tensoring with the vector space $N_{\bar x}$ is exact: choose a basis and it is a direct sum of copies of the identity. Thus the right side has zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$. Exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks imply the same vanishing for $C\otimes^L_{k_X}N$. This proves the claim, including on each stratum, without claiming that bounded complexes over $A$ or $A/I^n$ are perfect.

source.place: Remark 6.3.2 and Definition 6.3.1; the residue-field finite Tor observation used in det-lem-integral-models-stacks. The tensor/stalk identity is the filtered-colimit calculation just written out.

proof.text: Assume (a), and choose $C$ as in that condition. Only finitely many $H^q(C)$ are nonzero. Refine their finitely many constructible stratifications to one finite stratification: at each refinement use the fibre-product immersion $S\times_X T\to X$, whose image is the intersection, rather than merely a set-theoretic factorization. On each resulting stratum $S$, all cohomology sheaves of $C|_S$ are locally constant with finitely presented $k$-module values. Such an $S$ is Noetherian: locally it is a quotient of a Noetherian affine chart by an ideal, and it is quasi-compact because its image is constructible. Step 1 makes $K|_S$ locally complete over $B_S$. The comparison-pullback isomorphism identifies its residue reduction with $\nu_S^*(C|_S)$. The restricted étale complex is bounded and has finite Tor amplitude by step 2. Apply the local perfect-lifting lemma with coefficient ring $A$, ideal $I$ and scheme $S$. It supplies a pro-étale covering and bounded finite-projective $A$-complexes giving exactly the models in (b). Here $A\simeq\varprojlim A/I^n$ is an explicit hypothesis of the item; neither finiteness of $k$ nor perfectness of $A/I^n$ over $A$ has been used.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, forward implication, using Lemma 6.6.8; Stacks Tag 09C6 (lemma-connected-adic-lisse) gives the local lifting ingredient. Refining the already-given residue strata realizes the same local-to-stratified route.

proof.text: Assume (b). On a trivializing cover of a stratum the terms of a perfect model are direct summands of finite sums of $B_U=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_U$. More explicitly, if $P^q=eA^d$ for an idempotent $e$, then $B_U\otimes_A P^q=eB_U^d=\varprojlim_n e(A/I^n)_U^d$; finite products and the equalizer defining an idempotent image commute with limits. Each sheaf in the last tower is killed by $I^n$. The torsion-limit completeness lemma shows that the realized bounded complex is locally complete after restriction to constant $A$ coefficients. The constant/completed equivalence reflects completeness, so it is complete as a $B_U$-complex. Step 1 detects completeness globally. There are also global cohomological bounds: each stratum is quasi-compact, and the pro-étale covering axiom gives finitely many quasi-compact open pieces of the trivializing members that cover it. The restrictions to those pieces retain the same respective perfect models. Take the smallest and largest term degrees among the finitely many models on all the strata (use $[0,0]$ if $X$ is empty). Exact restriction and finite-stratum detection imply $H^q(K)=0$ outside this finite interval. This proves the boundedness assertion without using any dimension bound on $X$.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication, and Lemma 6.5.3; Stacks Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), power-torsion inverse limits and bounded complete complexes.

proof.text: Still under (b), the completed coefficient reduction lemma gives $B_U\otimes_A^L k\simeq k_U$ and hence identifies the reduction of every local model with the constant bounded complex $P^\bullet\otimes_A k$. Its terms are finite-dimensional vector spaces. The constant-module section lemma makes constant realization exact, so the cohomology of a constant complex is the constant sheaf of its cohomology. Tensoring a bounded complex of finite-projective $B_U$-modules with $k_U$ is computed termwise: its finite stupid filtration proves K-flatness, since tensoring an acyclic complex with a projective term is acyclic. The finitely many models selected in step 4 give a single cohomological interval for $K\otimes^L_{B_X}k_X$, detected globally by finite-stratum detection. On each stratum its cohomology is locally the constant cohomology of $P^\bullet\otimes_A k$, a finite-dimensional vector space. It is therefore intrinsically constructible. Apply the existing constructible comparison theorem for discrete Noetherian coefficients with $\Lambda=k$: the reduction is $\nu_X^*C$ for a bounded étale $k$-complex with constructible cohomology. The constructibility used by that theorem is affine-local [def-pe-etale-constructible-module], on the étale and on the pro-étale site; on the Noetherian scheme $X$ it is the global finite-stratification condition of (a) and of [lem-sfb-discrete-noetherian-constructible-serre]. Indeed, choose a finite affine cover $U_1,\ldots,U_m$ of $X$ by spectra of Noetherian rings. Each $|U_i|$ is a Noetherian space [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], hence so is the finite union $|X|$, and in a Noetherian space every finite union of locally closed subsets is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Global to local: for a stratification $(Z_k\to X)_k$ the fibre products $Z_k\times_XU\to U$ form a stratification of an affine open $U$, with images $T_k\cap U$ locally closed, hence constructible, in the Noetherian space $|U|$, and the restrictions stay locally constant. Local to global: put $W_i=U_i\setminus(U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_{i-1})$, locally closed in $X$, with its reduced induced subscheme structure in the open subscheme $U_i$. If $(Z_{ia}\to U_i)_a$ is the finite partition of $U_i$ supplied by the affine-local definition for one sheaf, the immersions $Z_{ia}\times_{U_i}W_i\to X$ have the pairwise disjoint images $Z_{ia}\cap W_i$ covering $X$; each is locally closed in $U_i$, hence in $X$, so constructible in $X$. Inverse image along $Z_{ia}\times_{U_i}W_i\to Z_{ia}$ keeps the sheaf locally constant with the same finitely generated, hence finitely presented, values. This gives a finite global stratification for each of the finitely many nonzero $H^q(C)$, and the same two arguments apply on the pro-étale site. Step 2 gives finite Tor amplitude for this bounded étale complex. Together with completeness from step 4 this proves (a).

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication; Stacks Tags 093M (sites-modules-lemma-completion-flat), 09AL (lemma-compare-constructible-derived), and 09B5 (lemma-constructible-serre).

proof.text: Finally, the completion unit of step 1 is a natural transformation between exact functors: derived tensor with each finite free Koszul complex is exact, and derived inverse limit is exact by the strict-tower lemma. Thus the cone of the unit vanishes at the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whenever it vanishes at two vertices, by the long exact cohomology sequence applied to the natural map of triangles. It vanishes for zero and commutes with shifts. The complete objects therefore form a full triangulated subcategory. Residue reduction is an exact triangulated functor by derived change of rings. By the existing constructible comparison theorem, its bounded objects with constructible étale origin are precisely the bounded objects with intrinsically constructible cohomology. By step 5, on the Noetherian scheme $X$ the affine-local constructibility of that theorem and the finite-stratification constructibility of (a) and of the weak Serre lemma are the same condition, on both sites. The weak Serre lemma for discrete Noetherian coefficients proves that this latter condition is closed under ambient cones: for any morphism $L\to M$ between such objects the long exact sequence identifies $H^q(\operatorname{Cone}(L\to M))$ as an extension of $\operatorname{coker}(H^qL\to H^qM)$ by $\ker(H^{q+1}L\to H^{q+1}M)$. Both sheaves, and therefore the extension, are constructible. The same sequence bounds the cone whenever L and M are bounded; rotating triangles gives the other two-out-of-three cases. Zero and shifts retain bounded constructible cohomology. Over $k$ the finite Tor condition adds no further restriction by step 2. Intersecting these two conditions proves exactly the asserted closure of (a) under zero, isomorphisms, shifts, and every ambient distinguished triangle.
